title: Embouchure covering both lips and Albert vs Boehm system
summary: Father's technique of covering the teeth, lip control, and why Dutre stayed on Albert system clarinet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And he tells about that he learned from your father to cover both lips. Do you do that? I never did notice when you played.

Well, my father taught me that way. I had to start that way. Do you still do that? No, I don't. You don't do that now? No. And after I got able to play some, he said, well, you don't have to cover each other teeth anymore.
Mm-hmm. Very few people do it. I think Barney Bigard does that.
He's about the only one that I've seen of the jazz musicians.
It's all right. But I think it's best that you start that way because you have more lip control. Now, if you just start with your teeth up there, I don't think you have too much power, lip control.
Well, did you start on the Albert system or Bain or Huchard?

Albert. On the old Albert. I stayed on the Albert. Never the change. Well, there wasn't any printing changing because I can play both systems, but I just wanted to show the fellas that you could get as much out of an Albert that you could do with a Bain.
Yeah. And most of the New Orleans fellas, almost all of them used it.
I guess. Yes, they did at the time when they came out, they started changing.

Yeah. Still, a lot of them used it. People like Edmund Hall and of course the fellas around here almost all use the Albert system too. Did you notice much difference in the two systems? In the tone, if there's any difference in tone? I know the keys are a little easier on the Bain.

There isn't any difference in the tone. The tone comes from the man. The only thing, the systems are not too much a part. B flat, B natural, F and F sharp, C and C sharp. Yeah. That's the only difference on this.

I wonder if there's much difference like in the bore or something. If some people told me the Albert system maybe is a little bit more, a bigger bore inside. And maybe some people think they can get a bigger tone now, the Albert. I wondered if you'd ever noticed anything like that.
Well, I have noticed that. But I seem to get the same tone from both instruments.
I should think most people would. Do you remember anything else about your lessons as your father?
